prompt: Why do they want to make an extension to the library?

options.text: It has had no renovation since it was founded.
It needs to double the number of computers.
There has been an increased number of visiting people.

evidence: The speaker describes growth in library use over the past ten years and says there is therefore a clear need for an extension.
why: The extension is justified by increased use of the library, which matches option C.
trap: A: The reason given is not the absence of renovation. B: New computers are mentioned as a recent improvement, not as the reason for needing the extension.
explanation: The library needs more space because more people are using it.

prompt: The investment from the city council will be used for
evidence: The speaker says the lighting is quite poor and that the city council has authorised spending in this area. The extra staff member is only an application awaiting a later decision.
why: The authorised council spending specifically refers to improving the lighting, so option C is correct.
trap: A: Extra staff recruitment has only been applied for and has not yet been approved. B: The eight new PCs were already installed earlier and are not the purpose of this investment.
explanation: The current authorised investment is for lighting improvements. The screenshot explanation conflicts with the audio and was corrected using the audio evidence.

prompt: According to Jack, why did Samuel Prout never become very famous?

options.text: He was seen as out of fashion.
His work never had a major exhibition.

evidence: Jack says Prout was prolific and never completely went out of vogue, but there was never a high-profile showing of his paintings that might have brought him wider attention.
why: The missing high-profile exhibition is the reason Jack gives for Prout not achieving greater fame.
trap: A: Jack explicitly says Prout was prolific. B: He says Prout never completely went out of vogue, so being simply out of fashion is not the explanation.
explanation: Prout lacked the kind of major exhibition that could have raised his public profile.

prompt: Dr Rubin and Jack agree that many of Prout's problems were caused by
evidence: They discuss Prout's chronic chest infections, which affected him throughout his life, while his wife, family, colleagues and supporters are described positively.
why: His recurring health problems are the shared explanation for many of the difficulties he faced.
trap: B: His colleagues and supporters are described as a strong network, not as jealous opponents. C: His wife and family are described as loving and supportive.
explanation: The conversation attributes many of Prout's difficulties to persistent ill health.

evidence: The speakers say Prout does not seem to have learned the skill from his father and that he painstakingly reproduced other painters' works.
why: Reproducing other painters' works means he learned by copying pictures, which matches option C.
trap: A: The conversation explicitly says he does not seem to have learned from his father. B: Visiting galleries is not given as the method by which he learned.
explanation: Prout developed his painting skills by carefully reproducing the works of other painters.
